_comment: Hand-curation verdicts, applied by scripts/build_site_table.py AFTER the
title keyword pass and overriding it. Each verdict names a human-checked
reason; the title pass stays visible in the source because its failures
are the reason this file exists.
A verdict goes in here only with evidence that is checkable from outside
the geometry -- construct provenance, citation, deposition metadata -- so
that labelling an entry can never be a restatement of the descriptor the
label is later used to test. The one class that matters for that is
natural_ln_biology: it is the positive class of the ROADMAP 3.17/3.19
contrast, so an entry promoted into it on the strength of its coordination
number would make that contrast circular.
Written by ROADMAP 3.19. Rebuild with: python -I scripts/build_site_table.py

classes.natural_ln_biology: A wild-type protein whose lanthanide site is the protein's own.
classes.ln_substituted_ca: A native calcium site holding a lanthanide instead.
classes.ln_substituted_native_site: A native site for some OTHER metal holding a lanthanide. Split out of ln_substituted_ca by 3.19, which could not express lactoferrin (Fe3+). The displaced metal is named in the basis.
classes.engineered_lbt: A designed or grafted lanthanide-binding construct: LBT fusions, de-novo binders, chelate conjugates, paramagnetic-NMR tags.
classes.phasing_artefact: The lanthanide is a reagent. Nucleating or phasing agent, heavy-atom derivative, or an adventitious surface ion.
classes.not_protein: The host polymer is not a protein. Breaks the axis the other four classes share -- they say what the SITE is, this says what the MOLECULE is -- and is here so that such an entry is visibly excluded rather than silently mislabelled.

evidence: The fourth natural family, and the one the title pass could not see: the titles say 'Structure of MIF binding with <element> ions' and contain no keyword. Only struct_keywords says 'Rare earth, Metalloprotein'.

Wild type, verified before use: construct = UniProt Q1H2G7 residues 23-175, the mature chain after the annotated signal peptide (the single mismatch is the initiator Met for Ala23). pdbx_mutation is empty. Methylobacillus flagellatus KT; E. coli is the expression host only. UniProt annotates two PepSY domains in tandem.

A real site rather than a soak: 159 sites over the 7 crystals reduce to 24 distinct residue signatures, and 5 of those occur in ALL SEVEN while 16 occur in exactly one. The 16 are the soak background; the 5 are the protein's own sites.
Seven crystals, seven different lanthanides (Yb, Tb, Ho, La, Sm, Gd, Nd), 1.21-3.05 A.
Citation: 'Adjacent Rare Earth Separation by a protein atomic ruler', to be published. Released 2026-07-22.
groups.not_evidence: The five conserved signatures are carboxylate-dominated -- four carboxylate-only, the fifth carrying a single Gln -- and the family's median coordination number is 9. Both are recorded here rather than above because they are descriptors the 3.17/3.19 contrast measures ON this family; admitting the family on them would make that contrast circular.
groups.consequence: Promoting these to the positive class is what took geometry from two criteria to one: the family reaches CN 9 through five MONODENTATE carboxylates, so the v1 bidentate>=2 criterion failed on it, and at the threshold that keeps it (>=1) 30 of 55 calcium accessions pass too.

evidence: The Tb-Xo4 'crystallophore' series: a lanthanide complex added as a nucleating and phasing agent to lysozyme, thaumatin, a phage tail protein, a protease, an adenylate kinase and a thiazole synthase. Ligand codes 7MT / WRT.
Right element, certainly not biology -- the converse of the calcium contrast, which tests the wrong metal in a real site. This tests the right metal in a non-site.

Ground truth for the negative control in 3.19: of their 126 sites, 98 are removed by the resolution and chelator filters and NONE of the surviving 28 reaches CN 9 (they run CN 0-4, other_ligand_donor_count 0 -- bare surface ions that the chelator flag correctly declined to fire on).

entry_notes.9B1V: 'Crystal structure of PqqT with PQQ and Gd3+ bound'. The study is engineered -- 'Structure-driven development of a biomimetic rare earth artificial metalloprotein', PNAS 2024, doi:10.1073/pnas.2405836121 -- but the three deposited Gd sites are CN 0-3, i.e. not the designed site.
entry_notes.9WE9: 'Plasmodium vivax aspartyl-tRNA synthetase in complex with L-Asp, Lanthanide, MOPSO and Butanetriol'. The title lists the lanthanide between a buffer and a cryoprotectant, and struct_keywords never mentions it. Three Yb sites on single surface glutamates (GLU474, GLU554 twice), CN 5-6.

evidence: Classed on what the deposited sites are rather than on what the paper is about; the provenance is recorded here so a later curator can disagree with that choice.

'Co-crystallization of streptavidin-biotin complex with a lanthanide-ligand complex gives rise to a novel crystal form'. Streptavidin is a biotin-binding beta barrel; the Tb arrives already chelated, as a crystallization additive. Same role as Tb-Xo4, different chemistry: the ligand here is pyridine-2,6-dicarboxylate (dipicolinate).

This is the entry on which the chelator filter is load-bearing. All 20 Tb sites are chelator-flagged and every one has protein_donor_count 0 -- the protein contributes nothing to any of them -- yet 8 reach CN 9 through the chelate alone. Without the filter those 8 are false positives for the v2 criterion. The Tb-Xo4 series never tested this: its 28 surviving sites run CN 0-4, so CN alone would have been enough for them.

'Crystal structure of the Awp3b (adhesin-like wall protein 3b) A-domain from Candida glabrata showing a gadolinium cluster'. An adhesin A-domain binds peptides and sugars; struct_keywords calls the lanthanide a 'gadolinium cluster' / 'lanthanide cluster' outright.

42 Gd sites in one deposition, 28 of them at CN 0-2 -- the soak background. The best is CN 8 (LYS109;ARG110;GLY139;GLU141;ASP169, a site with two cationic residues in its own first shell). None reaches CN 9.

'Crystal structure of core domain of four-domain heme-cupredoxin-Cu nitrite reductase from Bradyrhizobium sp. ORS 375' -- a copper enzyme. Neither title nor struct_keywords mentions a lanthanide at all; the entry is in the shortlist only because its organism matched, which is why that tier is called 'supporting'.

Four different rare-earth elements in one crystal (Er, Tb, Yb, and Y, which is a rare earth but not a lanthanide) across 30 sites at 2.87 A, every one of them CN 0-1. A phasing screen, and the clearest case in the corpus that an organism match on its own carries no weight.

'Crystal structure of the ternary EcoRV-DNA-Lu complex with uncleaved DNA substrate. Lanthanide binding to EcoRV-DNA complex inhibits cleavage.' EcoRV is a Mg2+-dependent restriction endonuclease; Lu3+ occupies the catalytic metal site and stalls the reaction, which is how the uncleaved substrate was trapped.

The two Lu sites sit on GLU45 and ASP74 -- the PD...D/ExK catalytic carboxylates themselves, not surface acid. A genuine metal site holding the wrong metal on purpose: the second displaced metal this class has had to express, after Fe3+ in lactoferrin.

Reported in ROADMAP 3.19 because it is the one site among these six entries that passes the v2 criterion (CN 9, 4 protein donors, 2 bidentate carboxylates, not chelator-flagged). It is a true positive for the score and a negative for the biology: the score ranks SITES that suit a lanthanide, and a catalytic carboxylate cluster does, whether or not the organism ever meets one.

'Solution structure of a lanthanide-binding DNA aptamer'. Organism 'synthetic construct', no UniProt accession, struct_keywords 'aptamer, lanthanide, DNA'. A selected nucleic acid, so neither natural protein biology nor a protein engineering construct -- the four original classes have nowhere to put it.

The parse confirms it from the coordinates rather than the metadata: the single Lu site's signature is DC15;DG17;DC18, three deoxynucleotides. It is also a parser limitation worth naming -- those three are counted in protein_donor_count, because the donor count keys on polymer residues and does not ask which polymer.

entry_notes.2RPV: 'Solution Structure of GB1 with LBT probe'.
entry_notes.9L6D: 'the crystal structure of Azurin-LBT' -- an LBT fusion, not a lanthanide-substituted copper site.

evidence: Both are lanthanide-binding-tag fusions that the title pass missed only because it does not key on the abbreviation 'LBT'. Adding the abbreviation to TITLE_RULES was rejected: as a bare three-letter substring it also matches ordinary words, and two hand verdicts are cheaper than a rule that needs its own false-positive audit.
Monoclonal antibody 2D12.5 Fab in complex with a DOTA-lanthanide chelate. The protein binds the cage, not the metal: all 4 sites are caught by the chelator flag independently of this label.
FKBP12-mTOR FRB-rapamycin complex with a lanthanide tag attached for pseudocontact shifts. The lanthanide reports on the structure; it is not part of it.

Human lactoferrin with Ce3+ in the iron sites ('diceric human lactoferrin'). This is the gap 3.19 found in the four-class scheme: the displacement is real and well documented, but the displaced metal is Fe3+, so ln_substituted_ca cannot express it.

confirmed_by_title_pass._comment: Checked by hand, title pass already right, no override written. Recorded so that 'not in verdicts' does not read as 'not looked at'.
confirmed_by_title_pass.1KSM: ln_substituted_ca via title:calbindin -- Ln-substituted calbindin D9k, used as a PCS system. The Ca-site label is the accurate one.
_comment_families: The 17 below are the three families of ROADMAP 3.17, vetted there and
not re-read here: this records that the title pass agrees with that
earlier reading, which is a weaker claim than a fresh per-entry check.
They carry no override, so their class_basis in the table stays the
title rule that produced it and none of them reads as curated.
confirmed_by_title_pass.6ZCV: natural_ln_biology via title:lanthanide-dependent -- MDH/XoxF. One Pr site and one Ca site; with 9PI2's two, these are the 3 calcium ions that 3.19 first miscounted into the lanthanide denominator.
confirmed_by_title_pass.9PI2: natural_ln_biology via title:lanm -- lanmodulin, and the single-crystal control of 3.18: 6 Nd sites and 2 Ca sites in one deposition
confirmed_by_title_pass.3LTQ: engineered_lbt via title:lanthanide binding tag -- 'Interleukin 1B solved by SAD using an inserted Lanthanide Binding Tag'. Engineered and used for phasing at once; the tag is the reason the metal is there, so the engineered label is the one that explains it.
confirmed_by_title_pass.5OBB: engineered_lbt via title:lanthanide binding motif -- 'a modified mouse H chain ferritin with a lanthanide binding motif'. 'Modified' is the deposition's own word.
